Casio

Casio is a Japanese electronics company known for its durable and innovative timepieces. It is widely recognized for pioneering digital watches and for its incredibly tough G-Shock line.

The story

Casio was founded in 1946 by Tadao Kashio and his brothers, initially producing mechanical parts and later achieving success with Japan's first electronic calculator. The company entered the watch market in 1974 with the Casiotron, the first digital watch with an automatic calendar. This innovation set the stage for decades of development in digital timekeeping, including the popular Vintage series and models with features like world time. A defining moment came in 1983 with the launch of the G-Shock, born from an engineer's desire to create a watch that wouldn't break when dropped. The G-Shock's revolutionary shock-resistant structure made it a global icon, leading to numerous variations like the classic square G-Shock 5600, the popular DW-6900, the rugged Rangeman, and the modern GA-2100 "CasiOak". The success of G-Shock also spawned the Baby-G line for women in 1994. Throughout its history, Casio has continued to innovate by creating specialized lines. The Edifice collection, introduced in 2000, offers a blend of dynamic design and advanced technology, often with a motorsport-inspired aesthetic. For outdoor enthusiasts, the Protrek series, which debuted in 1995, integrates sensor technology for measuring altitude, barometric pressure, and direction. Today, Casio maintains its position as a major player in the watch industry, known for its durable, feature-rich, and accessible timepieces across its diverse model lines.
